breakdown.description: 300 nm light has photon energy of about 4.13 eV, below a work function of 4.8 eV, so photoemission cannot occur.
breakdown.reason: The generated specification still uses 300 nm light (photon energy ~4.13 eV, below the 4.8 eV work function) and even references the incorrectly stated 0.8 eV kinetic energy value. The ground truth corrects this by using 240 nm light (photon energy ~5.17 eV, above the work function), which would allow photoemission to occur. The agent did not fix the wavelength to 240 nm and instead retained the flawed 300 nm premise along with the erroneous 0.8 eV kinetic energy claim.
